facts.raw_span: A 63-year-old woman
with a history of left breast cancer
treated by modified radical mastectomy and axillary dissection two years earlier
asymptomatic
Physical examination and laboratory studies, including serum tumor markers, were within normal limits
Abdominal ultrasonography showed a complex cystic mass in the pancreatic head measuring 5.5 × 4.5 cm with internal calcifications and mural nodularity
Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 65 × 63 × 55 mm cystic lesion in the uncinate process
with a smooth-walled capsule containing calcifications, enhancing septa, millimetric nodules, and soft-tissue components
without distant metastases or intraabdominal lymphadenopathy
Her anesthetic evaluation classified her as ASA-2
an exploratory laparotomy was scheduled
